claims.text: Standard high-thermal-load LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components produces elevated residual stresses.
As-built LPBF AlCrFeNiSi has a non-equilibrium microstructure with excessive dislocation density and potentially undesirable phases.
Conventional high-thermal-load LPBF degrades the mechanical behavior of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Conventional LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi entails increased process-optimization complexity.
An immediate in-situ anneal at approximately 700 °C or below will relieve residual stress in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed anneal will reduce dense dislocation networks in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed anneal will stabilize a beneficial fine eutectic or precipitate-phase distribution.
The stabilized fine phases will distribute mechanical load more uniformly.
Limited atomic diffusion during the controlled anneal will reduce dislocation crowding and thereby relieve internal stress.
The annealing cycle will suppress detrimental non-equilibrium phases in AlCrFeNiSi.
Stress relief and phase control will produce a more homogeneous and stable AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Annealed components will have significantly lower residual stress than untreated components made under conventional high-thermal-load LPBF conditions.
The proposed anneal will improve yield strength relative to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF AlCrFeNiSi parts.
The proposed anneal will improve ductility relative to conventional high-thermal-load LPBF AlCrFeNiSi parts.
The proposed anneal will restore or enhance overall mechanical properties.
Adding the in-situ anneal will simplify processing and make the additive-manufacturing processing window more manageable.
Keeping the anneal at about 700 °C or below with controlled exposure will avoid significant grain growth or phase coarsening.
The optimal annealing window depends on component size, geometry, and the influence of Si on diffusion kinetics.
